title: SDK Microcurriculum: 4-session labs + fault-injection manifest (draft)
content:
Purpose:
A compact, instructor-led microcurriculum (4 x 45–60m sessions) to get engineers from zero to instrumented SDK demos. Emphasis: reproducible sample apps, deliberate failure injection, and telemetried health checks so teams can confidently onboard to Redwood in 1 day. This doc is a working draft — experiments + notes for product/DE to iterate.

Audience:
- New integrator engineers (backend/frontend full-stack devs)
- Solutions engineers running 30–60m customer workshops
- DevExp facilitators who need a reproducible, low-friction sequence

Learning objectives (by end of 4 sessions):
1) Install and call Redwood SDK (JS + Python) in a sample app; see request/response and streaming.
2) Add retry/backoff and local failover using a lightweight stub.
3) Add telemetry: token-level cost attribution, latency traces, and error counters.
4) Run fault-injection scenarios (rate limiting, model fallback, KV cache misses) and observe graceful degradation + rollback.

High-level schedule (4 sessions):
- Session A (45m) — Quickstart and hello-loop
  - Goal: first request -> streaming -> basic prompt tuning example
  - Activities: repo clone, env var, run sample app (JS), verify output, open Console trace.
  - Checkpoint: participant can send a request and read latency/cost in Console.

- Session B (60m) — Resiliency and local stubbed workflows
  - Goal: demonstrate basic retry/backoff + local SDK stub for offline dev
  - Activities: integrate provided stub adapter, simulate 503 and see retry behavior, add circuit breaker toggle.
  - Checkpoint: participant can flip a toggle to force stub and run smoke tests.

- Session C (45m) — Telemetry and probe-driven alerts
  - Goal: emit and inspect telemetry for token usage, per-route latency percentiles, and prompt regression probes
  - Activities: wire SDK telemetry hook (quick config), run sample queries that trigger a regression test prompt set, view alerting mock.
  - Checkpoint: participant can correlate a slow request to a specific prompt and model variant.

- Session D (60m) — Fault-injection lab & rollback playbook
  - Goal: use fault-injection manifest to test fallbacks: model swap, region failover, dedicated->hosted substitution
  - Activities: run manifest (scripts) that injects rate-limit, full-GPU OOM surrogate, KV-cache coldstart; trigger canary rollback flow.
  - Checkpoint: participant runs manifest and performs an automated rollback to a compatible smaller model.

Lab artifacts (included in repo):
- repo: sdk-microlabs/ (root)
  - quickstart-js/ (hello-loop)
  - quickstart-py/ (hello-loop)
  - stub-adapter/ (local stub server + dockerfile)
  - telemetry-hooks/ (examples: prometheus exporter, simple file sink)
  - fault-manifests/ (yaml manifests to drive failure scripts)
  - smoke-tests/ (postman/curl scripts and expected outputs)

Failure scenarios to cover (manifest examples):
- soft-rate-limit: simulate 95th percentile rate-limiting, expect exponential backoff and degraded answers in content.
- model-fallback: kill primary model process -> route to smaller quantized variant; validate output quality probe triggers.
- kv-cache-warm: clear prefix cache -> observe token cost spike and longer latencies.
- region-outage: block region endpoint -> auto-route to fallback region with minimal data leak notes.
- streaming-cut: forcibly drop streaming connection -> client resumes using non-streaming response.

Telemetry checklist (what participants will validate):
- SDK emits request id and token counts per call
- Per-route latency histograms (p50, p95, p99) viewable in demo Console
- Error classification: transient vs permanent, with counters and sample traces
- Regression probe results logged to a simple csv and surfaced by alert mock

Instructor notes & facilitation tips:
- Setup (30m before): ensure Docker & node/python preinstalled; provide VM image for sticky participants.
- Use breakout pairs for Session B (one toggles stub, one observes Console).
- Keep failure manifest aggressive but reversible: all injected changes should have a single-script rollback.
- If time runs short: skip in-depth telemetry exporter and show pre-recorded dashboard.

Quick commands (for facilitator):
- Clone: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-microlabs.git
- Start stub: cd stub-adapter && docker build -t rwd-stub . && docker run -p 8080:8080 rwd-stub
- Run js quickstart: cd quickstart-js && npm ci && NODE_ENV=dev REDWOOD_API_KEY=redwood-test npm start
- Run fault manifest: ./scripts/run-fault-manifest --manifest fault-manifests/model-fallback.yaml
- Rollback: ./scripts/rollback-last || ./scripts/rollback-manifest --manifest fault-manifests/model-fallback.yaml

Evaluation rubric (fast, binary-friendly):
- Boot (1): Repo cloned and sample app started within 10m
- Call (1): Able to make a request and see a response within 5m
- Stub (1): Toggle to stub and back without manual code changes
- Telemetry (1): Able to find request in Console and read token attribution
- Fault (1): Run one fault manifest and execute rollback successfully
- Total passing score: 5/5 (goal: 80% of participants pass 4/5 in the first run)

Open questions / decisions to make (TODOs):
- Which model variants to include in model-fallback manifests? (Miguel to propose list: gpt-like-8b-q4, redwood-lite-3b)
- Default alerting medium: Slack vs web mock? (Sofia + Product)
- Should we add an optional Codelab for mobile (React Native)? (Priya to prototype)
- How many preseed credits to give per workshop to avoid hitting quotas? (Ops/Platform)

Notes to self (working + shorthand):
- keep sessions < 60m to fit into customer calendars
- provide downloadable VM image (ubuntu + docker) for slower setups
- add tiny CI job to ensure quickstart-js/quickstart-py start successfully every week (GH action)

Link references / anchors:
- demo repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-samples/pull/87
- linear: SDKS-212 (mini-lab failures)
- convo: #sdk-onramp slack thread (pinned instructions)

Next steps (owners):
- Miguel: draft model variant list + add to manifests (ETA 2024-11-01)
- Sofia: mock alert UI for telemetry probes (ETA 2024-11-08)
- Ethan: add GH action smoke test + CI job (ETA 2024-11-15)
- Priya: prototype RN quickstart if time allows (ETA 2024-11-29)

End of draft. This is intentionally prescriptive — meant to be iterated after first run.
